# VVIP TIGER — Final Business Model Conflict Inventory

**Decision:** VVIP-TIGER-BM-2026-07-25
**Branch:** feat/final-publishing-cards-model-20260725
**Scanned commit:** 7e0997f3ed7d9c877f51c8c19dfc9fb350847c45
**Generated:** 2026-07-25T08:36:08Z
**Mode:** Inventory only — no implementation deleted or modified.

## Authoritative interpretation

The platform provides publishing, search, discovery and direct communication.

The platform is not a seller, buyer, transaction broker, escrow provider,
shipping provider or payment intermediary for vehicle-part sales.

Payments are limited to approved publishing cards.

## Inventory summary

| Area | Matches | Required disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Currency conversion and rounding | 954 | Review; retain only publishing-card provider display and payment records |
| Commission, brokerage and seller payouts | 48 | Remove or replace when confirmed as conflicting |
| Vehicle-parts checkout and shopping cart | 0 | Remove or replace when confirmed as conflicting |
| Escrow, wallet, settlement and shipping | 3349 | Remove or replace when confirmed as conflicting |
| Publishing cards and subscriptions | 680 | Retain, normalize and complete |
| Database and migration references | 6707 | Review dependencies and migration safety |

## Classification rules

Every match must be classified before implementation changes:

- **KEEP:** compliant with the final decision.
- **MODIFY:** useful implementation whose semantics must be changed.
- **REMOVE_AFTER_PROOF:** conflicting and proven unused or safely replaceable.
- **HISTORICAL_DOCUMENT:** retained only as traceable history.
- **FALSE_POSITIVE:** unrelated match.
- **OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED:** unresolved business behavior.

No file, table, migration, route, test or component may be deleted merely because
its name matched a search term.

docs/launch/pr36/DECISIONS.md:15:| D09 | Concurrency 2; deadlines 20/120 seconds; debounce 250 ms. | Hung and stale work aborts and is disposed. |
docs/launch/pr36/FINAL_REPORT.md:5:PR36 adds local-only JPEG/PNG/WebP validation, bounded 4:3 processing, safe WebP/JPEG derivatives, concurrency/deadline scheduling, cancellation and stale suppression, transactional session ownership, reorder/cover/edit behavior, and an Arabic-first RTL controller integrated into PR31. PR32 retains bounded metadata only and PR33 clamps the count to seven. PR34 remains unchanged.
docs/launch/pr36/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md:5:Implemented a dependency-free, local-only seven-photo flow integrated with the PR31 listing shell. It accepts declared and signature-matching JPEG, PNG, and WebP sources; enforces count, compressed-size, decoded-dimension, pixel, crop, output, concurrency, timeout, cancellation, and safe-metadata boundaries; and does not upload or publish.
docs/launch/pr36/RED_GREEN_EVIDENCE.md:13:- Concurrency regression: exit 1 with observed maximum `1`, expected `2`.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:32:- Bounds are seven images, 15 MiB per source/derivative, 60 MiB per selection, 40 MP decoded, maximum 1600×1200, exact 4:3, concurrency two, 20-second job deadline, and non-extendable 120-second processing session.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:52:- Browser decoders and encoders remain platform components; their internal memory use and implementation vulnerabilities cannot be eliminated by JavaScript. PR36 limits compressed bytes, preflights pixels, caps concurrency/output, applies deadlines, closes resources, and fails closed, but does not claim a universal memory ceiling.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:73:- seven-photo, byte, header, pixel, timeout and concurrency limits;
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:22:| R3-PA-02 | Important | `cancelOperation()` only marked queued entries. If both slots were active, a matching queued promise remained pending until unrelated active work settled. A caller requesting cancellation therefore did not receive prompt deterministic settlement. | Matching queued entries are removed and rejected immediately with `cancelled`; matching active entries are aborted; disposal retains the same bounded cleanup path. The configured concurrency is clamped to the hard ceiling of two. | `scheduler.test.mjs`: prompt queued cancellation while two unrelated slots are occupied; configured concurrency `99` still observes maximum `2`; active worker cancellation coverage remains green. The pre-fix queued-cancel regression stalled until the test command was terminated. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:25:| R3-PA-05 | Important | A scheduler deadline only called `AbortController.abort()`. If a browser primitive ignored abort or never settled, the public job promise also never settled. A focused fake-clock reproduction advanced exactly 20,000 ms and observed `STILL_PENDING`, defeating both the per-photo deadline and transparent timeout semantics. Queued work behind two such jobs also had no independent session-deadline timer. | The scheduler now rejects the public promise with `processing_timeout` or `session_timeout` at the exact deadline, aborts the underlying job, ignores late settlement, and gives every queued entry an independent timer tied to the same non-extendable session origin. The two active slots remain reserved until underlying work actually settles, so replacement work cannot exceed concurrency two. Cancellation/disposal likewise reject callers promptly while aborting underlying work. | The identical untracked fake-clock reproduction now prints `processing_timeout`. Frozen `scheduler.test.mjs` remains green, including FIFO, hard concurrency ceiling two, queued/running cancellation, exact deadlines, zero timer cleanup, and idle-page origin. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:31:- Queue concurrency has a hard runtime ceiling of **2**, including when an injected caller requests `99`. FIFO behavior and maximum active count are observed by `scheduler.test.mjs`; selection processing independently observes maximum `2` in `session.test.mjs`.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:81:- Targeted searches for networking/connectivity APIs, modal/Tab traps, deadline constants, debounce, concurrency, memory ownership, and object-URL lifecycle were inspected. PR36 networking/connectivity matches were absent; deadline/debounce/concurrency matches were limited to the fixed policy/runtime/tests documented above.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:98:- FIFO scheduling with a maximum concurrency of two;
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_4_FINAL.md:66:Errors retain stable non-sensitive codes and calm Arabic-first copy; raw exceptions, filenames, object URLs, bytes, credentials, or identities are not projected into draft metadata or change events. Cancellation, stale results, validation failures, decode/encode failures, and timeouts fail closed without automatic retry. Automated contracts cover RTL ordering, keyboard operations, Escape/focus restoration, live regions, 44 px targets, reduced motion, 320 px layout rules, bounded local metadata, concurrency two, deadlines, and URL cleanup.

docs/specifications/VVIP_TIGER_GLOBAL_EXECUTION_SPEC_FINAL_AR.md:2948:- المستخدم يستطيع إنشاء إعلان بعملة وموقع وحقول مناسبة لقطاعه ودولته، ورفعه للمراجعة ونشره وإدارته.
docs/specifications/VVIP_TIGER_GLOBAL_EXECUTION_SPEC_FINAL_AR.md:3147:- إعداد نموذج أسعار قابل للتهيئة حسب الدولة والعملة.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:13:Exactly enforce: seven photos; JPEG/PNG/WebP only; 15 MiB each; 60 MiB selection; 40,000,000 decoded pixels; minimum 320×240; exact 4:3; maximum 1600×1200; no upscale; WebP 0.82 then JPEG 0.86; concurrency 2; 20-second photo and 120-second session deadlines; 250 ms debounce. Abort and suppress stale results. Revoke every URL. Cancel leaves no operation resource/reference; success discards every original `File`. No upload, publish, network API, persistence of bytes/URLs, remote/privileged operation, video, package change, tracked deletion, or intermediate commit. Arabic-first RTL, keyboard/mobile accessible, offline-capable, fail closed.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:56:**Interfaces:** `createScheduler({maxConcurrency,jobTimeoutMs,sessionTimeoutMs,clock})` with `enqueue/cancelOperation/dispose`; `createMediaSession(...)` with `select/beginEdit/previewEdit/confirmOperation/cancelOperation/remove/reorder/setCover/displaySnapshot/reset/dispose`.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:61:- [ ] Rerun; expect concurrency maximum exactly 2, zero pending timers, and `created=revoked+live committed` PASS.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:98:- [ ] **Round 3 performance/accessibility:** create `REVIEW_ROUND3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md`; observe concurrency, deadlines, resource balance, exact outputs, debounce, 320 px, RTL keyboard/focus/live regions/44 px/reduced motion. Make no universal memory/network claim.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-20-global-platform-control-plane-implementation.md:15:- Four-million registered-user year-one capacity target; test in 10k/25k/50k concurrency tiers.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:28:- Price: positive `numericPrice` with up to two decimal places and an ISO-style three-letter `currency`.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:25:| `pr36-scheduler.js` | FIFO concurrency two, deadlines, abort, stale suppression. |
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:39:- Concurrency: two. Photo deadline: 20 seconds. Non-extendable session deadline: 120 seconds. UI debounce: 250 ms.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:77:Injected fake files, clocks, decoders, canvases, URLs, and workers prove limits, geometry, fallback, concurrency, deadlines, cancellation, stale suppression, disposal, order/cover, metadata, and accessibility. Static guards reject forbidden capabilities. Browser smoke covers real formats, offline processing, keyboard/RTL, cancellation, worker/fallback, and resource cleanup without retaining fixtures.

project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:76:        "Global V1 — منصة عالمية متعددة الدول واللغات والعملات"
project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:244:    "text": "12. مصفوفة الدول واللغات والعملات"
project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:292:    "text": "الهدف النهائي هو إطلاق VVIP TIGER كمنصة عالمية واحدة تعمل من خلال نواة برمجية موحدة وقابلة للتهيئة حسب الدولة واللغة والعملة، مع سوق إعلانات متعدد القطاعات، ملفات شخصية، تواصل فردي، دعم ومراجعة، اشتراكات، إدارة عالمية، وبنية أمنية وتشغيلية قابلة للتوسع. لا تتعامل Global V1 بأموال الصفقات بين المستخدمين، بل تبيع اشتراكات وخدمات ترويجية للمنصة فقط."
project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:310:    "text": "المستخدم يستطيع إنشاء إعلان بعملة وموقع وحقول مناسبة لقطاعه ودولته، ورفعه للمراجعة ونشره وإدارته."
project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:985:    "text": "إعداد نموذج أسعار قابل للتهيئة حسب الدولة والعملة."

User ticket reads exclude internal notes and filter by requester at both the local projection and future trusted boundary.

docs/launch/pr35/CODEX_REVIEW_ROUND1.md:2238:  When submission fails while offline, this reports that the request is pending on the device, but the controller never invokes `createUserSubmissionQueue` or persists the payload anywhere. Closing or reloading the page loses the request and nothing is sent when connectivity returns, so either enqueue it before showing this state or report an ordinary failed submission.

docs/launch/pr35/CODEX_REVIEW_ROUND3.md:2784:  When the browser reports `navigator.onLine === true` but the request fails because of DNS, timeout, captive portal, or a dropped connection, the production adapter converts the exception to a failed result and this branch returns `failed` immediately. The submission is therefore not added to the permitted user queue even though the network is effectively unavailable, which is a common weak-network case. Treat transport/network failure codes as queueable independently of the unreliable online hint.

The submission is therefore not added to the permitted user queue even though the network is effectively unavailable, which is a common weak-network case. Treat transport/network failure codes as queueable independently of the unreliable online hint.

docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:21:| R3-PA-01 | Important | Source validation and image processing shared the same two-worker loop. With two valid slow files followed by an invalid third file, both processing slots blocked before the invalid file was inspected; validation feedback reached the test's 25 ms failure boundary instead of returning the stable validation code. | `select()` now completes bounded local source validation for the whole selection before starting any decode/encode work. On validation failure, collected source/header references are cleared and processing count remains zero. | `session.test.mjs`: `all validation feedback completes before any image processing starts`. RED was the 25 ms `validation_not_immediate` boundary with two processors already entered; GREEN returns `mime_not_allowed` with processor count `0`. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:22:| R3-PA-02 | Important | `cancelOperation()` only marked queued entries. If both slots were active, a matching queued promise remained pending until unrelated active work settled. A caller requesting cancellation therefore did not receive prompt deterministic settlement. | Matching queued entries are removed and rejected immediately with `cancelled`; matching active entries are aborted; disposal retains the same bounded cleanup path. The configured concurrency is clamped to the hard ceiling of two. | `scheduler.test.mjs`: prompt queued cancellation while two unrelated slots are occupied; configured concurrency `99` still observes maximum `2`; active worker cancellation coverage remains green. The pre-fix queued-cancel regression stalled until the test command was terminated. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:25:| R3-PA-05 | Important | A scheduler deadline only called `AbortController.abort()`. If a browser primitive ignored abort or never settled, the public job promise also never settled. A focused fake-clock reproduction advanced exactly 20,000 ms and observed `STILL_PENDING`, defeating both the per-photo deadline and transparent timeout semantics. Queued work behind two such jobs also had no independent session-deadline timer. | The scheduler now rejects the public promise with `processing_timeout` or `session_timeout` at the exact deadline, aborts the underlying job, ignores late settlement, and gives every queued entry an independent timer tied to the same non-extendable session origin. The two active slots remain reserved until underlying work actually settles, so replacement work cannot exceed concurrency two. Cancellation/disposal likewise reject callers promptly while aborting underlying work. | The identical untracked fake-clock reproduction now prints `processing_timeout`. Frozen `scheduler.test.mjs` remains green, including FIFO, hard concurrency ceiling two, queued/running cancellation, exact deadlines, zero timer cleanup, and idle-page origin. |

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:53:Create idempotency is scoped by owner and idempotency key. Update idempotency is scoped by owner, listing, and idempotency key. A repeated operation returns the first completed result. Listing identity, owner identity, and creation time are immutable during update.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:55:Pagination accepts a nullable opaque cursor and a requested limit. Limits default to 20, clamp to 1–50, and return `{ items, nextCursor, limit }`. The local cursor is the last listing ID; a remote implementation may use an opaque server cursor without changing the interface.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:9:PR35 adds a local-first, production-fail-closed foundation for owner governance, permission policies, scoped assignments, Tiger Care, and immutable audit records to the canonical static PR29–PR33 runtime. It does not deploy SQL, mutate Supabase or Clerk, implement payments, expose management telephone numbers, or claim delivery by an unconfigured adapter.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:71:`mode` is `local` or `production`. Production construction without a verified transport returns `CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED`; it never substitutes local success. Local mode may model operations for review but labels them local and never claims remote persistence or email delivery.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:93:Cancellation is valid only for the owner-isolated requester while no irreversible staff action exists, or for authorized staff with a reason. Reopening a resolution requires a reason and audit. Internal notes are a separate type and permission surface and are never returned by user-facing queries. User access is always constrained to `requesterId === actor.id` by the trusted production boundary.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:105:The account center gains a real Tiger Care entry. Canonical listing cards gain an accessible three-dot menu with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, keyboard navigation, Escape dismissal, focus return, and Tiger Care/report actions. The owner console is a separate `owner-control.html` route linked only after authorization; hidden navigation is not security. It uses landmarks, headings, visible focus, 44px targets, semantic tables/cards, live regions, dialog focus containment, reduced-motion media queries, and stable skeleton dimensions.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:59:Worker use requires successful probes for Worker, OffscreenCanvas, createImageBitmap, protocol, and output. A worker capability/runtime failure may fall back once to the main-thread adapter only while the job is current. This is not a retry of a rejected security decision. If both paths are uncertain, return `capability_unavailable`. The worker receives only transferred bytes, IDs, crop, and bounded policy and has no network, storage, cookie, filesystem, logging, DOM, upload, or publishing API.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-vvip-tiger-global-platform-and-p08-clerk-recovery-design.md:71:5. التوصيل.
docs/ux-r02/UX_R02_COMMUNICATION_AND_TIGER_CARE.md:3:Messages are local, text-only, and one-to-one. Group chat, broadcasts, real contacts, realtime delivery, and administrative reading claims are excluded. Private sharing is limited to a local counter of twenty invitees.

user-journey-preview/user-journey.js:16:function home(){const items=filtered();return `<section class="page-head"><div><p class="eyebrow">UNIFIED HOME</p><h1>كل ما تحتاجه، في مكان واحد.</h1><p>ابحث وتصفح وتواصل داخل منصة واحدة. القطاعات فلاتر وليست بوابات منفصلة.</p></div><button class="button primary" data-route="create">إنشاء إعلان</button></section><section class="panel"><label><span class="muted">بحث بسيط</span><input id="home-search" type="search" placeholder="ابحث عن قطع أو مواد أو عقارات" value="${esc(state.term)}"></label><div class="actions" style="margin-top:10px"><button class="button quiet" data-route="search">بحث متقدم</button><button class="button quiet" data-route="care">Tiger Care</button></div></section><section class="page-head"><div><p class="eyebrow">قطاعات المنصة</p><h2>إعلانات حديثة</h2></div>${sectorChips()}</section>${items.length?`<section class="cards">${items.map(listingCard).join('')}</section>`:empty('لا توجد نتائج','إزالة الفلاتر','reset')}<section class="grid" style="margin-top:16px"><article class="panel"><h3>محفوظات Mock</h3><p>عنصران محفوظان داخل هذه الجلسة.</p><button class="button quiet" data-route="market">فتح السوق</button></article><article class="panel"><h3>اقتراحات حسب المنطقة</h3><p>${PROFILE.region} · ${PROFILE.area}</p></article><article class="panel"><h3>Tiger Care</h3><p>الدعم المنظم دون رقم إدارة.</p><button class="button quiet" data-route="care">فتح الطلبات</button></article></section>`}

docs/specifications/VVIP_TIGER_GLOBAL_EXECUTION_SPEC_FINAL_AR.md:107:الهدف النهائي هو إطلاق VVIP TIGER كمنصة عالمية واحدة تعمل من خلال نواة برمجية موحدة وقابلة للتهيئة حسب الدولة واللغة والعملة، مع سوق إعلانات متعدد القطاعات، ملفات شخصية، تواصل فردي، دعم ومراجعة، اشتراكات، إدارة عالمية، وبنية أمنية وتشغيلية قابلة للتوسع. لا تتعامل Global V1 بأموال الصفقات بين المستخدمين، بل تبيع اشتراكات وخدمات ترويجية للمنصة فقط.

project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.json:292:    "text": "الهدف النهائي هو إطلاق VVIP TIGER كمنصة عالمية واحدة تعمل من خلال نواة برمجية موحدة وقابلة للتهيئة حسب الدولة واللغة والعملة، مع سوق إعلانات متعدد القطاعات، ملفات شخصية، تواصل فردي، دعم ومراجعة، اشتراكات، إدارة عالمية، وبنية أمنية وتشغيلية قابلة للتوسع. لا تتعامل Global V1 بأموال الصفقات بين المستخدمين، بل تبيع اشتراكات وخدمات ترويجية للمنصة فقط."

project-control/sources/VVIP_TIGER_Global_Execution_Specification_V2_AR.md:73:الهدف النهائي هو إطلاق VVIP TIGER كمنصة عالمية واحدة تعمل من خلال نواة برمجية موحدة وقابلة للتهيئة حسب الدولة واللغة والعملة، مع سوق إعلانات متعدد القطاعات، ملفات شخصية، تواصل فردي، دعم ومراجعة، اشتراكات، إدارة عالمية، وبنية أمنية وتشغيلية قابلة للتوسع. لا تتعامل Global V1 بأموال الصفقات بين المستخدمين، بل تبيع اشتراكات وخدمات ترويجية للمنصة فقط.

docs/launch/pr35/SECURITY_THREAT_MODEL.md:27:Out of scope for this PR: compromise of Clerk or Supabase infrastructure, production deployment, email provider delivery, payments, and physical insider coercion. These do not relax application controls.
docs/launch/pr35/TIGER_CARE_WORKFLOW.md:19:Routing filters active assignments by permission, scope, category/team eligibility, and current availability; it then uses deterministic least-open-ticket ordering with stable ID tie-break. No eligible assignee leaves the ticket unassigned and flagged for escalation. Urgent and fraud/safety requests enter the escalation lane without exposing internal classification to other users.

docs/launch/pr36/DECISIONS.md:15:| D09 | Concurrency 2; deadlines 20/120 seconds; debounce 250 ms. | Hung and stale work aborts and is disposed. |
docs/launch/pr36/DECISIONS.md:21:| D15 | Arabic-first accessibility is release-blocking. | RTL keyboard order/edit, focus, live status, 44 px targets, reduced motion, and 320 px layout require evidence. |
docs/launch/pr36/FINAL_REPORT.md:5:PR36 adds local-only JPEG/PNG/WebP validation, bounded 4:3 processing, safe WebP/JPEG derivatives, concurrency/deadline scheduling, cancellation and stale suppression, transactional session ownership, reorder/cover/edit behavior, and an Arabic-first RTL controller integrated into PR31. PR32 retains bounded metadata only and PR33 clamps the count to seven. PR34 remains unchanged.
docs/launch/pr36/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md:5:Implemented a dependency-free, local-only seven-photo flow integrated with the PR31 listing shell. It accepts declared and signature-matching JPEG, PNG, and WebP sources; enforces count, compressed-size, decoded-dimension, pixel, crop, output, concurrency, timeout, cancellation, and safe-metadata boundaries; and does not upload or publish.
docs/launch/pr36/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md:7:The runtime is split under `scripts/media/`. Browser primitives are injected into policy/session/canvas boundaries, while Node built-in tests exercise validation, geometry, adapters, scheduling, cancellation, resource ownership, reorder, cover, metadata, controller contracts, and integration.
docs/launch/pr36/MANUAL_BROWSER_EVIDENCE.md:7:Required owner-side verification remains: real JPEG/PNG/WebP and hostile formats; size/dimension/seven-item limits; crop/zoom/pan; ratio/no-upscale; reorder/cover; Arabic RTL keyboard and focus; cancel/reset/pagehide cleanup; offline processing; worker/fallback; timeout fixtures; zero media network requests; zero persistent bytes; and balanced object URLs.
docs/launch/pr36/RED_GREEN_EVIDENCE.md:13:- Concurrency regression: exit 1 with observed maximum `1`, expected `2`.
docs/launch/pr36/REVIEW_RESOLUTION_LOG.md:65:## Scope-order resume V7 — corrected final-gate ordering
docs/launch/pr36/REVIEW_RESOLUTION_LOG.md:71:V7 corrects the lifecycle order: all four reviews and gates run first, the fourth-round report is then written, and only afterward is the exact ten-file scope frozen and verified.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:18:- PR36 session state is the only live photo authority. It owns Files during validation, provisional and committed derivatives, object URLs, crop generations, order, cover, cancellation, and disposal.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:23:Both canonical pages load dependencies in the required order: signature → policy → geometry → canvas adapter → worker adapter → scheduler → session → controller → PR32 → PR31 → PR33. Redirect/history pages remain untouched.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_1_ARCHITECTURE.md:110:- Canonical pages load every PR36 dependency once and in order.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:32:- Bounds are seven images, 15 MiB per source/derivative, 60 MiB per selection, 40 MP decoded, maximum 1600×1200, exact 4:3, concurrency two, 20-second job deadline, and non-extendable 120-second processing session.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:52:- Browser decoders and encoders remain platform components; their internal memory use and implementation vulnerabilities cannot be eliminated by JavaScript. PR36 limits compressed bytes, preflights pixels, caps concurrency/output, applies deadlines, closes resources, and fails closed, but does not claim a universal memory ceiling.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_2_SECURITY_PRIVACY.md:73:- seven-photo, byte, header, pixel, timeout and concurrency limits;
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:22:| R3-PA-02 | Important | `cancelOperation()` only marked queued entries. If both slots were active, a matching queued promise remained pending until unrelated active work settled. A caller requesting cancellation therefore did not receive prompt deterministic settlement. | Matching queued entries are removed and rejected immediately with `cancelled`; matching active entries are aborted; disposal retains the same bounded cleanup path. The configured concurrency is clamped to the hard ceiling of two. | `scheduler.test.mjs`: prompt queued cancellation while two unrelated slots are occupied; configured concurrency `99` still observes maximum `2`; active worker cancellation coverage remains green. The pre-fix queued-cancel regression stalled until the test command was terminated. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:24:| R3-PA-04 | Important | The crop editor was exposed as `aria-modal="true"` and explicitly wrapped Tab focus, trapping the application even though the photo step is an optional part of a browsable page. Every cover/reorder/remove action also destroyed and recreated every photo node. | The editor is a labelled non-modal group; Tab follows document order; Escape/cancel closes and restores origin focus. List rendering retains keyed photo nodes and applies one ordered DOM batch. Cover state exposes `aria-pressed`; status/errors switch deterministically between polite `status` and assertive `alert`. Closing clears the exact 250 ms timer and preview source. | `controller-accessibility.test.mjs`: no modal/Tab trap, keyed node reuse, labelled 4:3 crop preview, Arabic/RTL controls, keyboard actions, 44 px targets, reduced motion, and 320 px mobile rule. The controller contract was RED before correction because modal/Tab-trap source remained. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:25:| R3-PA-05 | Important | A scheduler deadline only called `AbortController.abort()`. If a browser primitive ignored abort or never settled, the public job promise also never settled. A focused fake-clock reproduction advanced exactly 20,000 ms and observed `STILL_PENDING`, defeating both the per-photo deadline and transparent timeout semantics. Queued work behind two such jobs also had no independent session-deadline timer. | The scheduler now rejects the public promise with `processing_timeout` or `session_timeout` at the exact deadline, aborts the underlying job, ignores late settlement, and gives every queued entry an independent timer tied to the same non-extendable session origin. The two active slots remain reserved until underlying work actually settles, so replacement work cannot exceed concurrency two. Cancellation/disposal likewise reject callers promptly while aborting underlying work. | The identical untracked fake-clock reproduction now prints `processing_timeout`. Frozen `scheduler.test.mjs` remains green, including FIFO, hard concurrency ceiling two, queued/running cancellation, exact deadlines, zero timer cleanup, and idle-page origin. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:26:| R3-PA-06 | Important | Controller lifecycle and edit-event paths were not symmetric: `input` and `change` listeners on the crop group survived `dispose()`, a release/change flush did not clear its pending 250 ms input timer, and confirm could race that timer. Cover, remove, button reorder, and `Alt+Arrow` reorder updated the visual list without a specific live-region announcement. | Disposal now removes every listener it adds. Release/change and confirm clear the pending timer before one immediate local edit, and stale/cancelled preview races do not overwrite a newer success with an assertive error. Each list mutation emits calm Arabic status text through the existing polite live region. The approved non-modal group, normal Tab order, Escape cancellation, and focus restoration remain unchanged. | Frozen controller/integration tests pass; syntax passes. Source review verifies paired listener add/remove operations, one timer owner, polite mutation announcements, RTL logical ordering, and no new modal/focus behavior. |
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:31:- Queue concurrency has a hard runtime ceiling of **2**, including when an injected caller requests `99`. FIFO behavior and maximum active count are observed by `scheduler.test.mjs`; selection processing independently observes maximum `2` in `session.test.mjs`.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:38:- List updates reuse keyed `<li>`/image/control nodes and perform one ordered `replaceChildren(...ordered)` batch instead of rebuilding all descendants. Crop input processing is debounced rather than rendered on every input event.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:43:- Complete PR36 runtime searches and the focused forbidden-capability guard found no `fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, beacon, online/offline dependency, Supabase, Clerk, upload, or other network operation in the media path. Decode, crop, encode, ordering, cover selection, removal, cancellation, and metadata projection are local browser operations.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:50:- Keyboard users have native focusable controls for crop sliders/buttons, cover selection, before/after reorder, edit, remove, confirm, and cancel. `Alt+ArrowLeft/Right` reorders a focused photo; Escape cancels the crop; focus returns to the invoking input/button.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:52:- The selected-order list is labelled; crop preview and every control have calm Arabic labels; cover state is exposed with `aria-pressed`; normal progress is polite and errors are assertive. DOM order and Arabic `dir="rtl"` remain coherent.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:53:- Cover, removal, button reorder, and `Alt+Arrow` reorder changes now produce specific Arabic live-region announcements. Stale/cancelled preview work cannot replace a newer success announcement with an error.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:81:- Targeted searches for networking/connectivity APIs, modal/Tab traps, deadline constants, debounce, concurrency, memory ownership, and object-URL lifecycle were inspected. PR36 networking/connectivity matches were absent; deadline/debounce/concurrency matches were limited to the fixed policy/runtime/tests documented above.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md:98:- FIFO scheduling with a maximum concurrency of two;
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_4_FINAL.md:30:- `index.html` and `private-profile-p03.html` each load the PR36 stylesheet once and the eight page-side modules once in dependency order: signature, policy, geometry, canvas adapter, worker adapter, scheduler, session, controller. `pr36-media-worker.js` is intentionally instantiated only as a Worker and is not duplicated as a page script.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_4_FINAL.md:50:The complete diff contains no SQL, Supabase, Clerk mutation, service role, migration, package, lockfile, workflow, backup, deployment, or other production-boundary path. There is no tracked deletion. Suspect, historical, backup, migration, and uncertain artifacts remain preserved. No network, remote, privileged, upload, publish, payment, or video capability was added to the media runtime.
docs/launch/pr36/reviews/ROUND_4_FINAL.md:66:Errors retain stable non-sensitive codes and calm Arabic-first copy; raw exceptions, filenames, object URLs, bytes, credentials, or identities are not projected into draft metadata or change events. Cancellation, stale results, validation failures, decode/encode failures, and timeouts fail closed without automatic retry. Automated contracts cover RTL ordering, keyboard operations, Escape/focus restoration, live regions, 44 px targets, reduced motion, 320 px layout rules, bounded local metadata, concurrency two, deadlines, and URL cleanup.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-plan.md:287:## Planned execution order
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:13:Exactly enforce: seven photos; JPEG/PNG/WebP only; 15 MiB each; 60 MiB selection; 40,000,000 decoded pixels; minimum 320×240; exact 4:3; maximum 1600×1200; no upscale; WebP 0.82 then JPEG 0.86; concurrency 2; 20-second photo and 120-second session deadlines; 250 ms debounce. Abort and suppress stale results. Revoke every URL. Cancel leaves no operation resource/reference; success discards every original `File`. No upload, publish, network API, persistence of bytes/URLs, remote/privileged operation, video, package change, tracked deletion, or intermediate commit. Arabic-first RTL, keyboard/mobile accessible, offline-capable, fail closed.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:56:**Interfaces:** `createScheduler({maxConcurrency,jobTimeoutMs,sessionTimeoutMs,clock})` with `enqueue/cancelOperation/dispose`; `createMediaSession(...)` with `select/beginEdit/previewEdit/confirmOperation/cancelOperation/remove/reorder/setCover/displaySnapshot/reset/dispose`.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:58:- [ ] RED: fake-clock tests prove FIFO maximum 2, 19,999 ms success, 20,000 ms timeout, 120,000 ms session timeout, queued/running abort, no timers; session tests prove atomic commit, exact rollback, source release, stale disposal, balanced URLs, removal/reset/pagehide/dispose, order, cover, and metadata without URL/bytes/name.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:61:- [ ] Rerun; expect concurrency maximum exactly 2, zero pending timers, and `created=revoked+live committed` PASS.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:69:- [ ] RED: source/DOM tests require explicit MIME accept, ordered list, Arabic labels, edit/remove/cover/move, Escape, focus trap/restore, `Alt+Arrow`, live regions, 250 ms debounce/release flush, RTL, 44 px targets, reduced motion, 320 px rule; forbid `innerHTML`, logging, or byte/URL event detail.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:82:- [ ] GREEN: surgically replace the media section; recursively sanitize draft display metadata; preserve text draft; add ordered includes; change PR33 maximum 100 to 7.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:89:- [ ] Add syntax/tests, exact constants, forbidden network/storage/remote/video/logging/unsafe-sink guards, HTML order, exact manifest/freeze scope, PR33/PR34/PR35/smoke regressions, and whitespace. A `--self-test-guard` fixture containing `fetch("/forbidden")` must be rejected without modifying runtime.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:98:- [ ] **Round 3 performance/accessibility:** create `REVIEW_ROUND3_PERFORMANCE_ACCESSIBILITY.md`; observe concurrency, deadlines, resource balance, exact outputs, debounce, 320 px, RTL keyboard/focus/live regions/44 px/reduced motion. Make no universal memory/network claim.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing.md:109:- [ ] With `python -m http.server 800`, manually test both canonical pages: three formats; spoof/size/dimension/seven limits; crop/zoom/pan; exact ratio/no upscale; reorder/cover; keyboard/RTL/focus; all cancels/resets; offline; worker/fallback; timeout fixtures; DevTools zero media requests/persistent bytes and balanced URLs. Record browser/version without images.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-20-global-platform-control-plane-implementation.md:15:- Four-million registered-user year-one capacity target; test in 10k/25k/50k concurrency tiers.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-20-global-platform-control-plane-implementation.md:16:- Country and payment capabilities are disabled until approved.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:17:- A listing may describe at most seven ordered images. This contract stores metadata only.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:19:- No payment, upload, image processing, SQL, migration, Clerk mutation, or production Supabase operation is included.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:28:- Price: positive `numericPrice` with up to two decimal places and an ISO-style three-letter `currency`.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:32:- Media metadata: ordered `images` and nullable `coverImageId` referencing an image in that array.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr34-listing-contract-design.md:44:- Validation errors are stable objects ordered by canonical field order: `{ field, code, message }`.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:9:PR35 adds a local-first, production-fail-closed foundation for owner governance, permission policies, scoped assignments, Tiger Care, and immutable audit records to the canonical static PR29–PR33 runtime. It does not deploy SQL, mutate Supabase or Clerk, implement payments, expose management telephone numbers, or claim delivery by an unconfigured adapter.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-14-pr35-owner-control-tiger-care-design.md:121:No remote SQL or deployment, Clerk/Supabase mutation, service-role use, secret retrieval, payment, direct management phone, realtime transport, notification/email provider implementation, legacy tracked-file deletion, or claim that a disconnected network becomes fast.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:10:PR36 replaces the PR31 temporary photo behavior with a local-only workflow for up to seven still photos: selection, validation, 4:3 crop, zoom, pan, reorder, cover selection, confirm, and cancel. It performs no upload or real publishing. It adds no network, Supabase, SQL, migration, Clerk, service-role, payment, video, package, or production capability.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:25:| `pr36-scheduler.js` | FIFO concurrency two, deadlines, abort, stale suppression. |
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:26:| `pr36-session.js` | Transactional resource ownership, order, cover, disposal. |
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:39:- Concurrency: two. Photo deadline: 20 seconds. Non-extendable session deadline: 120 seconds. UI debounce: 250 ms.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:45:`createMediaSession({ validator, processor, scheduler, urls, ids, onChange })` exposes `select`, `beginEdit`, `previewEdit`, `confirmOperation`, `cancelOperation`, `remove`, `reorder`, `setCover`, `displaySnapshot`, `reset`, and `dispose`.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:63:Arabic/RTL is default and mobile-first. The input advertises only the three accepted MIME types, while runtime validation remains authoritative. The ordered photo list provides edit, remove, cover, move-before, and move-after buttons; `Alt+Arrow` provides logical RTL keyboard reordering. The first confirmed image becomes cover.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-15-pr36-secure-seven-photo-processing-design.md:77:Injected fake files, clocks, decoders, canvases, URLs, and workers prove limits, geometry, fallback, concurrency, deadlines, cancellation, stale suppression, disposal, order/cover, metadata, and accessibility. Static guards reject forbidden capabilities. Browser smoke covers real formats, offline processing, keyboard/RTL, cancellation, worker/fallback, and resource cleanup without retaining fixtures.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-vvip-tiger-global-platform-and-p08-clerk-recovery-design.md:144:5. Reorder واختيار Cover.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-vvip-tiger-global-platform-and-p08-clerk-recovery-design.md:384:7. Verify Clerk.load and mount order.

The preview intentionally contains no real authentication, users, tickets, messages, audit data, IP addresses, credentials, payments, subscriptions, accounting, RLS, SQL, migrations, storage, Clerk dashboard changes, server roles, Edge Functions, or network connectivity.

styles/vvip-pr35-owner-care.css:2:*{box-sizing:border-box}body.pr35-owner{margin:0;background:radial-gradient(circle at 80% 0,#dcebe5 0,transparent 35%),var(--pr35-bg);color:var(--pr35-ink);min-block-size:100vh}.pr35-console{inline-size:min(100%,1120px);margin-inline:auto;padding:20px 14px 90px}.pr35-gate{display:grid;place-items:center;min-block-size:100vh;padding:24px;text-align:center}.pr35-hero{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:16px;padding:22px;border-radius:24px;color:#fff;background:linear-gradient(145deg,#071b19,#0b5147);box-shadow:0 18px 50px #123c3324}.pr35-hero h1{margin:4px 0;font-size:clamp(1.65rem,7vw,2.8rem)}.pr35-hero p{margin:0;color:#d8e7e3}.pr35-hero a{color:#fff;min-height:44px;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;padding:0 14px;border:1px solid #ffffff55;border-radius:14px;text-decoration:none}.pr35-kicker{color:var(--pr35-gold);font-size:.72rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.12em}.pr35-disclosure,.pr35-status{padding:12px 14px;border-radius:14px;background:#fff7dc;border:1px solid #ead59c}.pr35-status:empty{display:none}.pr35-status[data-state=failed]{background:#fff0f0;border-color:#e8bcbc}.pr35-metrics,.pr35-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:12px;margin-block:14px}.pr35-metrics article,.pr35-panel{background:var(--pr35-paper);border:1px solid var(--pr35-line);border-radius:20px;padding:16px;box-shadow:0 8px 28px #153a3210}.pr35-metrics strong{display:block;font-size:1.55rem}.pr35-metrics span{color:var(--pr35-muted)}.pr35-heading{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:12px}.pr35-heading h2,.pr35-panel h2{margin:3px 0 12px}.pr35-search{display:grid;gap:6px;color:var(--pr35-muted);font-size:.82rem}.pr35-search input,.pr35-form input,.pr35-form select,.pr35-form textarea{inline-size:100%;min-height:44px;border:1px solid var(--pr35-line);border-radius:13px;padding:10px 12px;background:#fff;color:var(--pr35-ink);font:inherit}.pr35-form textarea{min-block-size:96px;resize:vertical}.pr35-form select[multiple]{min-block-size:132px}.pr35-filters{display:flex;gap:8px;overflow:auto;padding-block:12px}.pr35-filters button,.pr35-pagination button,.pr35-row button,.pr35-form button,.pr35-primary,.pr35-profile-actions button{min-height:44px;min-block-size:44px;border:1px solid var(--pr35-line);border-radius:12px;padding-inline:14px;background:#fff;color:var(--pr35-ink);font:inherit;font-weight:700;touch-action:manipulation}.pr35-filters [aria-pressed=true],.pr35-primary{background:var(--pr35-green)!important;color:#fff!important;border-color:var(--pr35-green)!important}.pr35-danger{background:var(--pr35-danger)!important;color:#fff!important}.pr35-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr auto;gap:6px 10px;align-items:center;padding:12px 0;border-block-end:1px solid var(--pr35-line)}.pr35-row span{color:var(--pr35-muted);font-size:.86rem}.pr35-row.is-warning{padding-inline:10px;border:1px solid #e1b25c;border-radius:12px;background:#fff8e8}.pr35-empty{color:var(--pr35-muted);padding:12px 0}.pr35-pagination{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:12px;padding-block-start:14px}.pr35-skeleton{min-block-size:72px;border-radius:14px;background:linear-gradient(90deg,#edf2f0 25%,#f8faf9 45%,#edf2f0 65%);background-size:200% 100%;animation:pr35-shimmer 1.4s infinite}.pr35-layer{position:fixed;z-index:1000;inset:0;inset-inline:0;display:flex;align-items:flex-end;justify-content:center;padding:12px;background:#06151299}.pr35-sheet{inline-size:min(100%,620px);max-block-size:min(90vh,780px);overflow:auto;background:#fff;border-radius:24px 24px 16px 16px;padding:20px;box-shadow:0 -16px 60px ## Mandatory next phase

1. Classify every candidate.
2. Map imports, routes, tests, schemas and runtime dependencies.
3. Produce a replacement and safe-removal manifest.
4. Create isolated specialist Worktrees.
5. Implement changes in controlled tracks.
6. Require tests and independent review before integration.
